messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — ACME escalated: ~4.8% of their streaming sessions in the last hour are showing as 5xx in billing. They say mobile clients are intentionally closing sockets mid-stream. We see gateway logs with "broken pipe" but some downstream logs show 499s. Customer is upset about being billed for 5xx.

alex_support: sample gateway log snippet:
```
2026-03-16T22:34:10Z gateway-12 ERR stream_write: write: broken pipe (EPIPE) conn=10.0.9.23 req_id=acf12
2026-03-16T22:34:10Z gateway-12 INFO classify_response: tunnel: upstream returned 499 client_closed req=acf12
2026-03-16T22:34:10Z gateway-12 WARN billing_label: labeled 5xx due to proxy-failure status=502 derived_from=halfclose heur=pc-EOF req=acf12
```

maya_sre: Can you attach the full request id and which gateway shard? I want pcap and request/response headers. Also which model/route?

alex_support: req_id=acf12, shard=gateway-12-us-east, route=/v1/stream/gen, model=redwood/gpt-stream-3b. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-support/acme/3012345678/ (link shared in thread).

liam_prodeng: Preliminary thought: our proxy half-close heuristic can rewrite certain EOFs into a gateway error (502) when upstream returns client-close, due to a recent change in connection teardown ordering (see commit 9d3a2b). That would explain why billing pipeline sees 5xx even though upstream was 499.

sophie_support: Customer-facing question — are we certain they were charged for those? Which billing pipeline label is used? If so we need to propose a credit and a temporary suppression while SRE investigates. :exclamation:

deploy-bot: deploy/gateway v3.14.2 -> prod completed 2026-03-16T21:50:02Z (sha 9d3a2b) :white_check_mark:

ingest-metrics-bot: alert: streaming.gateway.error_rate spiked to 4.8% for tenant=acme (rolling 1h) — anomaly detected. Graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/stream/tenant=acme

maya_sre: Repro steps I used locally (minimal):
```bash
# start a tiny chunked server that writes a few chunks then closes socket abruptly
python - <<'PY'
import socket, time
s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1',9001)); s.listen(1); c,a=s.accept();
c.send(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n5\r\nhello\r\n6\r\n world\r\n')
# close socket without sending final 0-length chunk
time.sleep(0.2); c.close(); s.close();
PY
# curl through gateway with no-buffering
curl -N --http1.1 http://<gateway>/v1/stream/gen -H 'Host: tenant-acme' --data-binary @- < <(printf 'prompt=hi')
```
I reproduced gateway log: EPIPE then gateway surfaced a 502 to the billing pipeline.

liam_prodeng: Thanks — that matches my suspicion. The commit changed the order of: send up final chunk -> close connection -> classify response. If the client closes before final chunk arrives, proxy code path raises EPIPE and we currently map that to a proxy failure (502) in the classifier. We should treat upstream 499 as client abort and not escalate to 5xx.

liam_prodeng: Immediate mitigation options:
- toggle per-route flag `disable_eof_classification=true` to treat abrupt EOFs as client-close instead of proxy-failure (no code deploy)
- roll back commit 9d3a2b (more disruptive)
- add a quick heuristic: if upstream status==499 or upstream logged client_close, map to 499 in billing (fast patch)

sophie_support: Recommend we flip the per-route flag for ACME and any tenants reporting similar spikes. Also propose credit: start with 10% of last invoice while we investigate. I'll draft support note once SRE confirms.

maya_sre: I applied `disable_eof_classification=true` to /v1/stream/gen for tenant=acme on gateway-12-us-east. Monitoring: will watch for billing-label flip.

ingest-metrics-bot: metric update: streaming.gateway.error_rate for tenant=acme dropped from 4.8% -> 0.4% within 2 minutes of config change.

liam_prodeng: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket with the minimal repro and suggested fix (prefer the quick heuristic mapping upstream 499 -> billing 499). Ticket INF-4821 created by customer_ops-bot. Attach repro and logs.

customer_ops-bot: JIRA INF-4821 created: "gateway: abrupt client EOFs misclassified as 5xx for chunked streaming" assigned to @liam_prodeng, priority P1.

alex_support: Action items summary:
- SRE (maya): monitor and collect any more samples (pcap/logs) from other tenants — in progress
- Eng-runtime (liam): triage INF-4821, patch heuristic or revert change — P1
- Support (sophie/alex): propose 10% credit to ACME and draft customer note after confirmation
- Billing (ops): hold auto-credits until ticket resolved (temporary suppression)

alex_support: I'll follow up with ACME now with a status update + ETA. Thanks everyone :heart:
